parts.title: A repair café in town
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, my cousin invited me to spend a weekend in a small seaside town. We travelled by coach because it was cheaper than the train, although the journey took longer. When we arrived, the weather was cloudy, so we visited the local museum first. I expected it to be rather boring, but a guide showed us old photographs of the harbour and explained how the fishing boats had changed over time.

The next morning was sunny. We hired bicycles and followed a path along the coast. The route was mostly flat, but we stopped several times to take photographs. At lunchtime, we bought sandwiches from a small shop and ate them on the beach. It was busy, but we found a quiet place near the rocks.

On Sunday, we planned to take a boat trip. Unfortunately, the sea was too rough, so the trip was cancelled. The owner gave everyone a refund and suggested a walk to a lighthouse instead. I was disappointed at first, but the view from the top was wonderful. I would happily return, especially if I could stay for a few more days.

The final section goes uphill towards a lighthouse. [4] On clear days, you can see several islands from the top. The council hopes to extend the path next year. [5]

turns.text: Welcome to the Hilltop Hostel. The front door is locked after eleven, so please take your key with you. Breakfast is served in the dining room from half past seven. parts.title: An interview with a town planner
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Nina, what do you write about?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: I write travel articles for a website. I started by sending photographs and short reports to a local newspaper.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you choose a place to visit?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: I read about its history first, but I also ask local people what they enjoy doing.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What is the hardest part of your job?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Sometimes the weather changes my plans. I once travelled to a village to write about a festival, but heavy rain meant the outdoor events were cancelled.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What do you enjoy most?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Meeting people and discovering places I would never find in a guidebook.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What advice would you give a new writer?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Keep a notebook, take clear photographs and check every detail before you publish.
